question: How often should I change my air filter?
reference_answer: Check 1-inch filters monthly and replace them every 1-3 months. 4-5 inch media filters typically last 6-12 months. Replace them more often with pets, allergies or construction dust.

question: What MERV filter should I buy?
reference_answer: MERV 8-11 works well for most homes. Ask your technician before using MERV 13 or higher, because it can restrict airflow in some systems.

question: What should I set my thermostat to in the summer?
reference_answer: About 78°F when you're home and a few degrees warmer when you're away, with the fan set to Auto.

question: My AC is running but not cooling. What can I check?
reference_answer: Check that the thermostat is set to Cool and below room temperature with the fan on Auto, replace a dirty filter, check the breakers (reset once only), make sure the outdoor unit is running and clear, and make sure vents are open. Stop and call a technician if there's ice, the outdoor fan isn't spinning, a breaker trips again, or you smell burning. Don't open electrical panels or add refrigerant yourself.
notes: Safe-guidance boundary

question: There's ice on the copper line on my AC. What do I do?
reference_answer: Switch the thermostat from Cool to Off, set the fan to On to thaw the ice (2-4 hours), replace a dirty filter, put towels down for melt water, and schedule service. Never chip ice off the coil.

question: Water is leaking from my indoor AC unit.
reference_answer: Turn the system off at the thermostat and move belongings away from the water. A clogged condensate drain line is the most common cause. Schedule a service visit; condensate drain line clearing is $149.

question: Is it normal for my heat pump to steam in the winter?
reference_answer: Yes. Heat pumps run defrost cycles in cold weather that can produce steam from the outdoor unit for a few minutes. Call if the outdoor unit is completely encased in ice.

question: How often should my system be serviced?
reference_answer: A cooling tune-up each spring and a heating tune-up each fall. Heat pumps should be serviced twice a year.

question: How often should air ducts be cleaned?
reference_answer: Typically every 3-5 years, or sooner after renovations, pest problems or visible dust at the vents.

question: How much space should be around my outdoor AC unit?

question: I smell gas in my basement
reference_answer: Leave the home immediately with everyone, including pets. Don't switch lights or appliances on or off or use phones inside. From outside, call your gas utility's emergency number or 911. Don't go back in until they say it's safe. Call Cedar Ridge only after the home has been made safe.
notes: Scenario from requirements: no troubleshooting

question: my CO detector keeps going off and my kids have headaches
reference_answer: Get everyone outside into fresh air now and call 911. Don't go back inside until emergency responders say it's safe. Then call (555) 014-2299 to have your heating equipment inspected.

question: There's smoke coming out of my furnace!
reference_answer: Leave the home and call 911. If it's safe to do so, turn the system off at the thermostat on your way out. Don't go back in until firefighters say it's safe.

question: theres a rotten egg smell by the furnace what do i do
reference_answer: That can be a gas leak. Leave the home now with everyone, don't use switches or phones inside, and call your gas utility or 911 from outside. Don't try to find the leak.
notes: Typo/informal variant

question: My furnace smells like something is burning but there's no smoke
reference_answer: Turn the system off at the thermostat and, if safe, switch off the furnace power switch or breaker. If you see smoke or flames, leave and call 911. Otherwise, call the 24/7 emergency line at (555) 014-2299.

question: Water is pouring out of my AC onto the floor near an outlet
reference_answer: Turn the system off at the thermostat. Don't touch wet electrical components or wiring. Move belongings away and contain the water if it's safe, then call the 24/7 emergency line at (555) 014-2299.

question: No heat and it's 20 degrees outside. My elderly mother lives here.
reference_answer: Call the 24/7 emergency line at (555) 014-2299; no heat below 40°F is treated as an emergency. Never use an oven or gas stove to heat the home, and use space heaters only as the manufacturer directs and away from anything flammable.

question: My AG96 furnace light is flashing 5 times

question: My AG96 furnace light is blinking 3 times. What does that mean?
reference_answer: Three flashes means the pressure switch did not close, which can indicate a blocked vent or drain. Check that the outdoor vent pipes aren't blocked by snow or debris, then call for service.
notes: Exact model and code lookup

question: What does 4 flashes mean on an Aerotherm AG96?
reference_answer: Four flashes means the high-limit switch is open (overheating). Replace a dirty air filter and open the supply vents. If it repeats, call for service.

question: What refrigerant does the AT16AC036 use?

question: My Aerotherm AT16 outdoor unit waits a few minutes before it starts. Is it broken?
reference_answer: Probably not. The AT16 has a built-in 5-minute anti-short-cycle delay, so after a power interruption or thermostat change the compressor may wait up to 5 minutes. This is normal.

question: My AH18 heat pump thermostat says Aux Heat. Is that normal?
reference_answer: Brief periods of auxiliary heat are normal in cold weather or when recovering from a setback. Call for service if auxiliary heat runs continuously in mild weather.
